input.plan:
# Hide admin nav from non-admins

## Cause

Access control is already correct:

- [`auth_status()`](relocation_jobs/core/auth.py) returns `user.is_admin` from `is_user_admin()`
- [`setAdminNavVisible()`](relocation_jobs/static/js/auth.js) sets `hidden` from `user.is_admin`
- [`/admin` APIs](relocation_jobs/core/auth.py) still 403 non-admins via `admin_required`

The leak is CSS. Both admin controls live in [`relocation_jobs/static/index.html`](relocation_jobs/static/index.html) with `hidden`, but later rules force them visible:

- `.header-secondary-btn { display: inline-flex }` — header **Admin** button
- `.user-dropdown-admin { display: block }` — account-menu **Admin panel** link

Those class selectors beat the user-agent `[hidden] { display: none }`, so the links show even when JS leaves `hidden` set. Clicking still 403s.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  status["GET /api/auth/status"] --> js["setAdminNavVisible is_admin"]
  js --> attr["hidden attribute"]
  attr --> css["display rules win"]
  css --> leak["Non-admin still sees Admin"]
```

## Approach

Keep the existing JS gate. Do not inject/remove DOM nodes or change who `is_user_admin` is.

Fix CSS so `hidden` wins, matching the pattern already used for `.user-dropdown[hidden]`:

```css
.header-secondary-btn[hidden],
a.admin-header-btn[hidden],
.user-dropdown-admin[hidden] {
  display: none !important;
}
```

Bump the panel stylesheet query in [`relocation_jobs/static/index.html`](relocation_jobs/static/index.html) (`styles.css?v=88` → `v=89`) so browsers pick up the rule.

This is already in the working tree from the earlier pass, plus tests:

- [`tests/web/test_admin_e2e.py`](tests/web/test_admin_e2e.py) — markup starts `hidden`; CSS has the overrides; JS only unhides on `user.is_admin`; regular-user `/api/auth/status` has `is_admin: false`
- Admin `/api/auth/status` still asserts `is_admin: true`

On confirm: verify those files, re-run the three test modules, leave git uncommitted.

## Out of scope

- Who counts as admin (`PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS` / `users.is_admin`)
- `/admin` HTML is public; APIs stay the real gate
- No deploy/commit unless you ask
